1	import AVFoundation
2	import AppKit
3	
4	/// The grants a screen recording stands on — each grant's read, the step a
5	/// press takes, the pane URLs and the sentences — values a probe can call.
6	/// A pure move out of `RecordingSetup.swift` under road map "creator-jobs"
7	/// CU0a's toll U1; `RecordingSetup+Camera.swift` extends `RecordingGrant`
8	/// with the camera's grant.
9	
10	// MARK: - The grants
11	
12	/// Decision 4 (road map 3 §0): the PANEL asks for the grants, the tool never
13	/// does — the rule the speech grant's `canAsk` carried, for two grants.
14	/// What lives here is the READ of each grant, the STEP a press takes, the
15	/// pane URLs and the sentences — all pure: nothing here prompts or opens;
16	/// `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()`, `AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess` and
17	/// the pane's `NSWorkspace.open` are called by the recorder panel alone
18	/// (`RecorderPanelController+Grants.swift`), because a system prompt needs
19	/// a person in front of it. A press asks for Screen Recording ONCE and
20	/// opens the pane on every later press (spec §11 recording) — but only in
21	/// a launchd-owned launch: a shell-launched press always asks, because TCC
22	/// gives that prompt to the terminal (R0 q1). A denied or restricted
23	/// microphone opens its pane; `.notDetermined` asks.
24	///
25	/// **Both refusal sentences are COMPUTED, and end with `launchClause` when
26	/// it is non-empty** (R1 review, unjudged and upheld): R0 q1 measured that
27	/// a shell-launched Frame Job is attributed by TCC to the TERMINAL, so a
28	/// person who followed the pane sentence and granted Frame Job.app would have
29	/// granted the wrong application and be refused again with no way to tell
30	/// why. The pane sentence stays the PREFIX — `recording_proof.py` matches
31	/// on it — and the clause names the launching process's pid.
32	enum RecordingGrant {
33	    /// `CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess()` — true when this PROCESS may
34	    /// capture. R0 q1: a shell-launched binary is attributed by TCC to the
35	    /// terminal, so from a proof this reads the terminal's grant, not the
36	    /// app's.
37	    static var screenRecordingGranted: Bool { CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess() }
38	
39	    /// The pane sentence alone — the prefix of `screenRecordingRefusal`.
40	    static let screenRecordingPaneSentence =
41	        "Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ "
42	        + "Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch."
43	
44	    static var screenRecordingRefusal: String { screenRecordingPaneSentence + launchClause }
45	
46	    /// Empty for an app launched by launchd (`open -a`, the Finder, the
47	    /// Dock — ppid 1, responsible for itself); otherwise the sentence that
48	    /// says whose grant this process is actually running under. `getppid()`
49	    /// is the cheapest true reading: R0 q1's `responsibility_get_pid_
50	    /// responsible_for_pid` is private API, and the parent is what TCC
51	    /// follows for a process launched from a shell.
52	    static var launchClause: String {
53	        let parent = getppid()
54	        guard parent != 1 else { return "" }
55	        return " This Frame Job was launched by another process (pid \(parent)), so the grant "
56	            + "that counts is that application's — the terminal's, for a shell launch; or "
57	            + "relaunch with open -a \"Frame Job\"."
58	    }
59	
60	    /// `AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus(for: .audio)`. Read BEFORE any
61	    /// `AVCaptureDeviceInput` is made: that initializer auto-prompts on
62	    /// `.notDetermined`, which is exactly the prompt the tool may not put up.
63	    static var microphoneStatus: AVAuthorizationStatus {
64	        AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus(for: .audio)
65	    }
66	
67	    /// The status as the framework spells it, for a message a script can
68	    /// read — `Transcriber.name(of:)`'s shape.
69	    static func name(of status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> String {
70	        switch status {
71	        case .notDetermined: return "notDetermined"
72	        case .restricted: return "restricted"
73	        case .denied: return "denied"
74	        case .authorized: return "authorized"
75	        @unknown default: return "unknown"
76	        }
77	    }
78	
79	    /// Names the status word and the one action that changes it: a
80	    /// `notDetermined` grant is asked for by pressing Record in the panel (the
81	    /// only place that may prompt), a denied or restricted one is turned on
82	    /// in System Settings. `launchClause` follows, on the same terms as the
83	    /// screen sentence's.
84	    static func microphoneRefusal(_ status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> String {
85	        let head = "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: \(name(of: status))). "
86	        switch status {
87	        case .notDetermined:
88	            return head + "Press Record in File ▸ New Recording… once to grant it." + launchClause
89	        default:
90	            return head + "Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone, "
91	                + "then relaunch." + launchClause
92	        }
93	    }
94	
95	    // MARK: The step a press takes
96	
97	    /// What a press of Record does about one grant: go on, put up the
98	    /// system prompt, or open System Settings at the grant's pane.
99	    enum Step: Equatable {
100	        case proceed
101	        case ask
102	        case openPane
103	    }
104	
105	    /// True when launchd is the parent (`open -a`, the Finder, the Dock) —
106	    /// the reading `launchClause` makes, so the two cannot disagree.
107	    static var launchedByLaunchd: Bool { getppid() == 1 }
108	
109	    /// Screen Recording: granted goes on; a shell launch always asks (its
110	    /// prompt is the terminal's, R0 q1, so `asked` means nothing there);
111	    /// a launchd-owned press that has asked before opens the pane; else ask.
112	    static func screenStep(granted: Bool, asked: Bool, launchedByLaunchd: Bool) -> Step {
113	        if granted { return .proceed }
114	        if !launchedByLaunchd { return .ask }
115	        if asked { return .openPane }
116	        return .ask
117	    }
118	
119	    /// The microphone, when one is chosen: authorized goes on,
120	    /// `.notDetermined` asks, and denied, restricted or unknown opens the
121	    /// pane — the system never prompts twice for it.
122	    static func microphoneStep(_ status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> Step {
123	        switch status {
124	        case .authorized: return .proceed
125	        case .notDetermined: return .ask
126	        case .denied, .restricted: return .openPane
127	        @unknown default: return .openPane
128	        }
129	    }
130	
131	    /// System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording.
132	    static let screenRecordingPaneURL = URL(
133	        string: "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ScreenCapture")
134	
135	    /// System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone.
136	    static let microphonePaneURL = URL(
137	        string: "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Microphone")
138	
139	    /// System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Camera (camera-recording CR1c).
140	    static let cameraPaneURL = URL(
141	        string: "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_Camera")
142	
143	    /// What a note adds once the pane has been opened.
144	    static let paneOpenedSentence = " System Settings is open at that pane."
145	
146	    /// The screen note after the pane opened: the pane sentence stays the
147	    /// PREFIX, and `launchClause` stays last.
148	    static var screenRecordingOpenedNote: String {
149	        screenRecordingPaneSentence + paneOpenedSentence + launchClause
150	    }
151	
152	    /// The microphone note after its pane opened: the refusal's head and
153	    /// fix, the opened sentence, then `launchClause`.
154	    static func microphoneOpenedNote(_ status: AVAuthorizationStatus) -> String {
155	        "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: \(name(of: status))). "
156	            + "Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Microphone, then relaunch."
157	            + paneOpenedSentence + launchClause
158	    }
159	
160	    // MARK: Input Monitoring (road map creator-jobs CU6, spec §11 CU-3, CU-62)
161	
162	    /// `CGPreflightListenEventAccess()` — whether this process may listen to key-downs (CU-S1
163	    /// `grant_api=cg`). A shell launch reads the terminal's grant, as Screen Recording does.
164	    static var inputMonitoringGranted: Bool { CGPreflightListenEventAccess() }
165	
166	    /// CU-3's sentence: no "then relaunch" (CU0b measured none is needed).
167	    static let inputMonitoringPaneSentence =
168	        "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ "
169	        + "Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring."
170	
171	    /// `record_screen`'s and the recorder's refusal: the pane sentence, then `launchClause`.
172	    static var inputMonitoringRefusal: String { inputMonitoringPaneSentence + launchClause }
173	
174	    /// What the panel's note adds: no prompt shows and Frame Job is not listed until a person
175	    /// adds it (CU0b, the owner's JOB-29 run).
176	    static let inputMonitoringAddSentence = " If Frame Job is not in its list, add it with +."
177	
178	    /// The panel's note after a press: the pane sentence, the add sentence, the opened sentence
179	    /// when System Settings opened, then `launchClause`.
180	    static func inputMonitoringNote(opened: Bool) -> String {
181	        inputMonitoringPaneSentence + inputMonitoringAddSentence
182	            + (opened ? paneOpenedSentence : "") + launchClause
183	    }
184	
185	    /// Input Monitoring: `screenStep`'s table — granted goes on; a shell launch always asks; a
186	    /// launchd-owned press that has asked before opens the pane; else ask (CU-62).
187	    static func inputMonitoringStep(granted: Bool, asked: Bool, launchedByLaunchd: Bool) -> Step {
188	        if granted { return .proceed }
189	        if !launchedByLaunchd { return .ask }
190	        if asked { return .openPane }
191	        return .ask
192	    }
193	
194	    /// System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring.
195	    static let inputMonitoringPaneURL = URL(
196	        string: "x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_ListenEvent")
197	}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The documentation site (`docs/site/`) against the tree. No app, no build, no network, stdlib
only; `pnpm build` in `docs/site/` is what proves the site renders and its links land.

A user-visible change has to reach the site, and nothing about the site's build notices a menu
item or an agent tool it has never heard of. These rows do:

  D1  every page has a title and a description;
  D2  the sidebar and the pages are one-to-one;
  D3  every feature in `src/data/features.json` names a page, and an anchor that page has;
  D4  every product tool in `AgentCatalog*.swift` has a heading on an `mcp/` page, and no dev tool
      (`AgentServer+DevTools.swift`) is named anywhere;
  D5  every menu item in `AppDelegate+*Menu*.swift` and `EditorViewController+GraphicMenus.swift`
      is on a reference page;
  D6  no page names something internal: a decision ID, a road map, an `rc_*` export, a source
      file, a dev launch default;
  D7  no page or data file holds a local path;
  D8  every `<Shot>` names a capture that exists in both looks;
  D9  no page uses the words `docs/site/CLAUDE.md` bans.

    python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py                       # the tree (make test)
    python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages a.mdx b.mdx   # those pages: D1, D6–D9
    python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --selftest            # CONTROL + M1..M9

`--selftest` copies the site's inputs to `tools/proof/work/docs_site/` and requires the copy to
show no problem (CONTROL), then nine mutants, each on a fresh copy, to show a problem in exactly
its row. Exit 0 when all hold, 1 otherwise.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys

ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", ".."))
SITE = os.path.join(ROOT, "docs", "site")
WORK = os.path.join(ROOT, "tools", "proof", "work", "docs_site")
SOURCES = os.path.join(ROOT, "app", "Sources")

# A menu's own title is not an item, and macOS writes these rows' text itself.
MENU_SKIP = {"MainMenu", "Services", "Open Recent"}

# Decision IDs by prefix. AC-3 is an audio format, so AC is not among them.
INTERNAL = (
    (re.compile(r"\b(?:AI|AP|AS|AU|CAM|CJ|CO|CU|CX|FC|GR|HD|MC|MT|NM|PR|PUB|REC|RMP|SH|SR|SW|SY|TL"
                r"|TR|TU|TX|VR)-\d+\b|\bG-\d{1,3}\b"), "a decision ID"),
    (re.compile(r"§\s?\d"), "a spec section"),
    (re.compile(r"\broad ?map\b", re.I), "a road map"),
    (re.compile(r"\brc_[a-z_]+"), "an rc_ export"),
    (re.compile(r"-RCDev|FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"), "a dev default"),
    (re.compile(r"app/Sources|core/src|tools/proof|\b\w+\.swift\b|\b\w+\.rs\b"), "a source file"),
    (re.compile(r"(?<![\w&/#])#\d{3}\b"), "an issue number"),
)
LOCAL_PATH = re.compile(r"/Users/[a-z]|/private/(?:tmp|var)|/var/folders/")
BANNED = re.compile(r"\b(?:seamless(?:ly)?|effortless(?:ly)?|robust|powerful|simply|supercharge"
                    r"|unleash)\b", re.I)
FENCE = re.compile(r"^```.*?^```", re.M | re.S)


def content_dir(site):
    return os.path.join(site, "src", "content", "docs")


def pages(site):
    """{slug: path} for every page, the home page's slug being ''."""
    found = {}
    base = content_dir(site)
    for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(base, "**", "*.md*"), recursive=True):
        slug = os.path.relpath(path, base).rsplit(".", 1)[0]
        found["" if slug == "index" else slug] = path
    return found


def split_page(text):
    match = re.match(r"---\n(.*?)\n---\n(.*)", text, re.S)
    return (match.group(1), match.group(2)) if match else ("", text)

Preview (first 2KB):
### Units and ids

- **Times are ticks, 600 000 per second.** One second is 600000, and one
  frame at 30 fps is 20000. Every time you send is rounded to the project's
  frame grid.
- **Clip, track, marker and media ids share one number space**, so an id
  names one thing on its own. `get_project` lists them.
- **`tracks[0]` is the back of the layer stack**, the bottom lane of the
  timeline. A higher index draws in front.
- **Clip and canvas colours are four numbers**, `[r, g, b, a]`, each 0–1.
  Three numbers, or a component out of range, is refused rather than filled
  in or clamped. A chroma key's colour, `video.chroma.key`, is `[r, g, b]`.
  Other colours are spelled differently: a marker's `color` and a clip's
  `label` are colour names such as `"red"`, and a graphic's colour props are
  hex strings such as `"#ff5a36"`.
- **A boolean** may also be sent as `"true"`, `"1"`, `"false"` or `"0"`.
- **Two shorthands:** `add_text_clip`'s `text` may be a plain string (the
  words), and `add_shape_clip`'s `shape` a plain string (the kind).
- **Some keys must be sent even when null**, because null means something:
  `set_transition`'s `kind` (null removes the transition) and
  `add_zoom_action`'s `region` (null zooms back out). Leaving either out is
  refused.
- **Speed rates are clamped, not refused.** `set_speed` and
  `add_speed_ramp` bring a `rate` outside ×0.1–×1000 into that range; a rate
  of zero or less is refused.
- **No list argument may be empty.** An empty `clips`, `ranges`
  (`ripple_delete_ranges`) or `groups` (`paste_attributes`) is refused by
  name. A frame-rate term of 0 in `set_canvas`'s `fps` is refused too.

## The tools

One hundred and two tools, grouped by area. A tool marked *op* is one of the
project's edit operations and also takes `scope`. Every tool takes
`project`. The tool's own description, which the client shows the model,
spells out each argument; the area pages cover the features in depth.

## Limits

- Only programs running as you can connect, and only while Frame Job is
  running (the helper launches it for a call).
- Calls run one at a time. A long call — an export's start is quick, but a
  recording or a transcription is not — holds the next one until it ends,
  and any call waits while you hold the mouse down mid-drag.
- If Frame Job launches but does not start listening within 60 seconds, the
  call is answered with that, and later calls in the same client session do
  not launch another copy; quit the stray copy and try again.
- A tool call never asks you anything, so anything that needs a question
  answered or a system grant given has to be done by a person first.
- Copy MCP Command writes the Claude Code command only; other clients take
  the helper's path by hand.
89-- **Corner** (the default) puts the camera in the bottom-right corner, scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % guide of **View ▸ Safe Areas**. **Rounded Corner** and **Circle** are the same corner with rounded edges or a circle. **Side by Side** puts the screen and the camera next to each other, and **Camera Full** fills the canvas with the camera.
90-- The layout starts at the camera clip's first frame. The screen keeps its full picture until the camera arrives, and the layout reaches no further than that stretch's screen clip or its camera clip, so a clip that was already in the project never moves, and another stretch's screen without a camera stays full.
91-- If a stretch's screen clip isn't playing where its camera starts, that camera goes in the bottom-right corner instead.
92-- With **Remove the camera's background when it lands** ticked, the camera's clips then get **Clip ▸ Remove Background** as their own undo step, **Remove Background**, before any [Enhance the microphone](#enhancing-the-microphone) and the boxes under [When it lands](#when-it-lands). Edit ▸ Undo takes it off and keeps the recording.

120-While the recording records shortcuts, a keyboard mark **⌨︎** follows the ● or ❚❚, in the menu bar's own colour, and the menu starts with a greyed-out **Recording keyboard shortcuts** row and a separator, recording or paused. This holds for a recording an agent started too.
121-
122-The item keeps one fixed width, so the other menu-bar items don't shift as the seconds tick. It's a little wider when it shows the keyboard mark. It comes down as soon as the recording stops.
123-
124-### Pausing and stopping
125-
126-You can pause, resume and stop from any of these places:
127-
128-- the menu-bar item's menu
129-- **File ▸ Pause Recording**, directly under New Recording…, which reads **Resume Recording** while paused and works only while a recording runs (it has no shortcut)
130-- **File ▸ Stop Recording** (⌥⌘N). While any recording runs, including a paused one, **File ▸ New Recording…** reads **Stop Recording** and stops it.
131-
132-The welcome window's **New Recording…** button never stops a recording. During a screen recording it only beeps, so use **File ▸ Stop Recording** or the menu-bar item. During a camera recording or a voice-over it shows the panel again.
133-
134-macOS's own screen-recording indicator in the menu bar can also stop the recording. Frame Job keeps what was captured and adds it.
135-
136-If you choose **Quit Frame Job** (⌘Q) during a recording, Frame Job doesn't quit. Instead it opens the menu-bar item's menu so you can stop or resume first. For a camera recording or a voice-over, it shows the panel instead.
137-
138-### Paused recordings are stretches
139-
140-A pause ends the current file and a resume starts a new one, so a paused recording is several files, one for each stretch between a start or resume and a pause or the stop. Each file is named by the time its stretch began. When the recording lands, the stretches sit end to end on one track, touching, with no transition between them. Each stretch's microphone file goes on the Microphone track, lined up with its own picture.
141-
142-The paused time is in no file. The elapsed time counts only what was recorded.
143-
144-## Where it lands
145-
146-When you stop, the panel's button reads **Stopping…** and then **Adding…** while the files are written and imported.
147-
148-### Into an open project
149-
150-The recording goes into the project you chose in **Record Into**, at its playhead, in whatever container is open (inside a nest if you're working in one):
151-
152-- The picture goes on the front track if it fits there. If not, Frame Job adds a new track in front of everything.
153-- The microphone goes on a new back track named **Microphone**.
154-- Everything is one undo step, **Add Recording**. Undo removes the clips and media entries but leaves the files on disk, just as undoing Add Media… does.
155-- The new clips are selected.
156-
157-If you're in the middle of a drag in that project when the recording stops, Frame Job waits for the drag to end before adding the recording, for up to 20 seconds. After that it gives up, and the panel names the files, which are on disk either way.
--
369:## For agents: `record_screen`
370-
371-`record_screen` records for a fixed number of seconds, then lands the result exactly as the panel does: into the target project at its playhead, or as a new project when no project is open. A new project is named after the recording's file and is addressed as `project: <the recording's path>`, the path `get_project` reports for it.
372-
373-There's no countdown: the recording starts at once, and the call blocks for `seconds` plus about a second, returning once the recording is finished, imported and placed. Slow file writers can hold it up to about 75 s more, and 60 s more for each further stretch of a paused recording. A timeout names the movies, which may still finish on their own.
374-

376-|---|---|---|

380-| `camera_format` | With `source: "camera"`, or with `camera` beside the screen, the format to record at: as `camera.format` spells it (`1920x1080@30`), or `WIDTHxHEIGHT` for that size's highest frame rate, or `best`, in any case. | `best` |
381-| `display` | Index of a shareable display, 0 being the main one. Can't be used with `window`. | 0 |
382-| `window` | A window id to record on its own. Can't be used with `display`. | — |

384-| `system_audio` | Record system sound into the movie. | true |

164	With `source: "voice_over"`, the default microphone is implied. The arguments `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing`, `keys`, `cursor` and `microphone: false` are refused by name.

166	With `source: "camera"`, Frame Job records a camera on its own, with no screen, into `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov`. The camera is the one `camera` names, or else the default camera: the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in camera, then the first one connected. It records at the camera's best format (the largest size wider than tall that runs at 30 fps or more, at that format's highest frame rate), or at the format `camera_format` names. A blank or null `camera_format` means best, and a format the camera doesn't have is refused with a list of the camera's formats. `microphone: true` adds the default microphone as a second file, as for a screen recording. The arguments `display`, `window`, `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows`, `keys`, `cursor`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` and `rate` are refused by name, and `camera` and `camera_format` are refused with `source: "voice_over"`. An unknown camera is refused with a list of every camera connected, and with none connected the answer is "No camera is connected." A camera recording needs the **Camera** permission (**System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Camera**), which is read and never asked for, like the others. The recording starts once the camera has settled at its frame rate (up to a second), and `seconds` counts from its first frame. A camera recording made this way takes the camera from the panel's preview: while it runs, the panel's **Preview** reads "The camera is recording." and the picture comes back when the recording ends. The answer carries `camera` with the camera's `name`, `id` and `format` (for example `1760x1328@30`), plus `problem` when the camera stopped on its own and `note` when it hadn't settled at its rate by the time recording began. The note repeats both. The movie has no sound of its own, so `has_audio` is false. In a new project, the canvas is the file's size at the format's frame rate.
167	
168	With `source: "screen"` (the default) and `camera`, Frame Job records that camera **beside the screen**, at the same time, for a talking head over a screencast. Each stretch of the recording gets a camera movie named after its screen movie, for example `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov`, at the camera's best format or the one `camera_format` names (`camera_format` without `camera` is refused: "With source screen, camera_format needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen."). The camera files land in the same undo step as the screen's, on one new track named **Camera** in front of everything. Each camera clip starts where its screen clip starts, moved by that stretch's measured `camera_offset`: the camera usually starts a little before the screen, so the clip's first frames are trimmed off rather than the clip starting early, and a camera clip never starts before its screen clip or overlaps the one before it. Each camera clip is laid out in `camera_layout` (`corner_square` by default, the **bottom-right corner**: scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % guide of **View ▸ Safe Areas**; or `corner_rounded`, `corner_circle`, `side_by_side`, `camera_full`) by one `switch_layout` at its first frame with its stretch's screen clip, as in [A camera beside the screen](#a-camera-beside-the-screen). It's an ordinary clip, so you can move or resize it. With `camera_cutout: true` the camera clips then get Remove Background as their own undo step, **Remove Background**, before any `enhance`, and the answer carries `camera_cutout` (`{clips}`) or `camera_cutout_error` ("No camera clip landed on the timeline, so Remove Background did not run."). Both are refused without `camera` ("With source screen, camera_layout needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen."), with `source: "voice_over"` and `"camera"`, and with `place: false` ("camera_layout lays out the landed camera clips, so it needs place: true."), all before any permission. The microphone, when asked for, lands on its own track as usual. With `place: false` the camera files are added to the media list only. In a new project, the first screen movie is the document, and its camera (with any microphone) is one undo step named **Add Camera**, or **Add Camera and Microphone**. Each entry of `segments` then also carries `camera_path`, `camera_duration` and `camera_offset` (ticks, positive when the camera began after the screen), `camera_problem` and `camera_note` when something went wrong with that stretch's camera, and `camera_media` and `camera_clip` when known. The camera is looked up, and the Camera permission checked, before the Screen Recording permission. The wait after the recording allows about 105 s more, and 90 s more for each further stretch, because each camera file is read too, and a timeout names the camera files after the movies. The panel's **Record the camera too** box, with a display or a window, makes the same recording, and its **Layout** and Remove the camera's background box are `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout`.
169	
170	**An agent never asks for a permission.** `record_screen` never shows a system prompt, never opens the window picker and never opens System Settings. The Screen Recording permission, and the Microphone permission when one is needed, must already be granted, usually by pressing Record in the panel once. A missing Screen Recording permission is refused with a sentence naming its System Settings pane. A missing Microphone permission is refused with its status (`notDetermined`, `denied` or `restricted`): when it was never answered, the sentence says to press Record in **File ▸ New Recording…** once; otherwise it names the Microphone pane. With `keys: "shortcuts"`, a missing Input Monitoring permission is refused with "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring." The order is the caller's own mistakes first (`keys` outside `off` and `shortcuts` among them, read after `include_framejob_windows`, then `cursor` outside `separate` and `in_picture`), then the Microphone permission, then Input Monitoring, then `project`, then the Camera and Screen Recording permissions. When Frame Job was launched from a shell, each refusal also names the launching process (its pid) and says to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"` or grant the terminal.
171	
172	Refusals come in a fixed order. The caller's own argument mistakes come first, so they're answered even without any permission: `seconds` missing or out of range, then `source` and the arguments that source refuses (`camera` and `camera_format` included), `display` with `window`, an unknown `rate` or `size`, an unknown `keys` or `cursor`, `enhance` without a microphone or with `place: false`, `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` or `speed_up_typing` with `place: false` and the last two without `keys: "shortcuts"`, `microphone` without the Microphone permission, and a `project` that names nothing open. A camera recording, or a screen recording with `camera`, then looks up the camera, then its `camera_format`, then checks the Camera permission. A screen recording then checks the Screen Recording permission, and only then looks up the display or window. When the screen is locked or every display is asleep, the refusal says so: "No display is shareable right now — the console is locked or every display is asleep; nothing can be recorded until one is."
173	
174	While an agent records, the same menu-bar item appears, so a person at the Mac can pause, resume or stop it. A person's Stop from the menu-bar item or the File menu ends the call early and the recording still lands, with `stopped_by: stopped` and a `duration` shorter than `seconds`. Starting a second recording while one runs is refused with "A recording is already in progress." Pausing shortens what the call records, because `seconds` is wall-clock time.
175	
176	The answer includes `path` (the first file), `duration` (the total recorded), `segments` (one entry per stretch), `pauses` (how many times Pause was pressed), `stopped_by` (`stopped`, `user_stopped` for macOS's own indicator only, or `system_stopped` when a display slept or a camera stopped on its own), `landed` (`document` or `new_project`), the new media and clip ids, `mic_offset`, `mic_problem` and `unreadable` when relevant, and a `note`. See [MCP](mcp.md) for the full tool reference.
177	
178	With `enhance: true`, the call lands the recording as usual and then waits, up to 5 minutes, for the microphone's sound to be analysed, then runs `enhance_voice`'s own steps on the microphone's clips at −16 LUFS (an agent's target never comes from the Normalize row; call `enhance_voice {target_lufs}` afterwards for another). It's its own undo step, **Enhance Voice**, as in [Enhancing the microphone](#enhancing-the-microphone). The answer then also carries `enhance`, the answer `enhance_voice` gives, or `enhance_error`, a sentence saying why it didn't run: nothing measurable (`Nothing could be enhanced. …`), no microphone clip on the timeline, or not analysed within 5 minutes. `project` is read after it. `enhance` is checked right after `place`, before any permission: `enhance: true` without a microphone is refused with "enhance: true enhances the microphone's clip, so it needs microphone: true (or source voice_over).", and with `place: false` with "enhance: true needs place: true — with place: false the microphone lands as media with no clip to enhance."
179	
180	With `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` or `speed_up_typing`, the call then runs `auto_zoom`, `add_shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing`, in that order, on the recording's screen clips, each as its own undo step as in [When it lands](#when-it-lands). An agent's runs use those tools' defaults (Zoom ×2, Lead 0.6 s, Stay 2.5 s, Follow on, Motion blur 50 %; bottom and dark overlays; ×4 for stretches of 3 s or more, Keep pitch on), never the sheets' remembered values, and `speed_up_typing` waits up to 5 minutes for the speech. The answer then also carries each one's own answer under its name, or a sentence under `auto_zoom_error`, `shortcut_overlays_error` or `speed_up_typing_error`: no screen clip with a cursor file landed, the project busy (or the speech not detected) within 5 minutes, the call stopped first, or the tool's own refusal, which an agent is told rather than asked (a speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 applies and says so in `audio_note`). `project` is read after them. They're checked right after `enhance`, before any permission, in that order: `place: false` is refused first ("auto_zoom: true plans on the landed screen clips, so it needs place: true."), then `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing` without `keys: "shortcuts"` ("speed_up_typing: true needs keys: \"shortcuts\" — without it the cursor file records no typing to speed up.").
181	
182	*Agents:* `record_screen` (`seconds`, plus the options above). There is no MCP tool for pause or resume. Those are a person's actions.
183	
184	## Limits
185	
186	- The panel records displays, single windows, a camera on its own, and a camera beside a display or a window. A camera records at one of its formats at that format's highest frame rate (not at a lower rate within the format's range). The panel lays a camera beside the screen out in one of five layouts, a corner always the bottom-right one; it has no control for another corner, Stacked, Screen Only, scale or inset. The layout's crop centres on the camera's picture, not on the person. There's no keystroke or callout overlay.
187	- When a stretch of a screen recording is left out because its movie can't be read, its camera file stays on disk and is named with its other kept files, but it isn't added to the project. Only that stretch's microphone is.
188	- There's no global shortcut to stop. Use the menu-bar item or the File menu.
189	- While a screen recording runs, the menu-bar item is the only place to pause or resume besides the File menu. If macOS hides the item, for example behind the notch or in a crowded menu bar, **File ▸ Stop Recording** and **File ▸ Pause Recording** still work.
190	- A recording longer than 9:59:59 shows a label wider than the item was sized for.
191	- When a project is already at its track limit, a recording that needs a new track can't be added. The files stay on disk and the note names them.
192	- If the screen is locked or every display is asleep, no display can be shared, so nothing can be recorded until one wakes.
193	- Record shortcuts writes nothing while any app holds secure input, and a typing mark is a time alone: there's no mode that records what you type.
194	- A **Separate** stretch whose cursor file couldn't be written (the screen never reported its start, or the file couldn't be saved) has no pointer at all: it isn't in the movie and there's nothing to draw it from. The landing's note says so, ending "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."
195	
196	See also: [Audio](audio.md) for setting the microphone and system-audio levels, [Export](export.md) for writing the finished edit, and [Menus and shortcuts](menus-and-shortcuts.md).

---
title: "Record with record_screen"
description: "How an agent records the screen, a camera or a voice-over for a set time and lands it in a project: every argument, answer and refusal."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

`record_screen` is **File ▸ New Recording…** without the panel. An agent says how many seconds to record, the call runs for that long, and the recording lands in the project the way one made with the panel does. There's no countdown, and the tool never asks for a permission.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs={[
    'Screen Recording permission, for a screen recording',
    'Microphone, Camera or Input Monitoring, only when the call uses them',
    'A person has to give each permission first',
  ]}
/>

## Record the screen

The smallest call names only `seconds`:

```json
{ "seconds": 30 }
```

That records the main display for 30 seconds with its system sound, leaves Frame Job's own windows out of the picture, and lands the movie at the playhead of the front project. A recording then goes through these stages:

- **It starts at once.** There's no countdown and no panel.
- **It writes to disk.** The file goes to `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, named for example `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22.mov`, and it's never stored inside the project. A name that's already taken gets ` (2)`, ` (3)` and so on.
- **It lands.** The movie becomes ordinary media, and a clip goes at the playhead on the front track of whatever is open, a [nest](/mcp/nests/) included. When that track has no room there, Frame Job adds a new track in front of everything. This is one undo step, **Add Recording**.
- **It answers.** The call returns once the recording is finished, imported and placed. See [What it answers](#what-it-answers).

With no project open, the recording opens as a new untitled project instead, and `landed` reads `new_project`. Its canvas takes the movie's size and `rate`. Later calls address that project with `project` set to the recording's path, which is the path `get_project` reports for it. If the target project closes while the recording runs, the same thing happens and the note says so.

Only one recording runs at a time, whoever started it. A second one is refused with "A recording is already in progress."

:::note
The built-in [Assistant](/assistant/what-it-will-not-do/) can't call `record_screen`. Recording stays with a person at the Record button, or an agent connected from outside.
:::

[Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) has the landing in full, and it's the same for both.

## Choose a source

`source` says what's recorded.

| `source` | What it records | Files |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `screen` | A display or a window. The default. | `Screen Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |
| `voice_over` | The default microphone alone, with no picture. | `Voice-over <date> at <time>.m4a` |
| `camera` | A camera alone, with no screen. | `Camera Recording <date> at <time>.mov` |

An argument the source can't use is refused by name, not ignored. A JSON null counts as not given. This is what each source takes:

| Argument | `screen` | `voice_over` | `camera` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seconds`, `project`, `path`, `place`, `enhance` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `microphone` | Yes | Implied, and `false` is refused | Yes |
| `rate` | Yes | Yes, for a new project's canvas | Refused |
| `camera`, `camera_format` | Yes, [beside the screen](#record-a-camera-beside-the-screen) | Refused | Yes |
| `camera_layout`, `camera_cutout` | Yes, with `camera` | Refused | Refused |
| `display`, `window`, `size`, `include_framejob_windows` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
| `system_audio`, `show_clicks`, `cursor`, `keys` | Yes | Refused | Refused |
| `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` | Yes | Refused | Refused |

## The arguments

Only `seconds` is required. The sections further down cover the arguments for [voice-overs](#record-a-voice-over), [cameras](#record-a-camera-alone) and the [steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands).

### Length and source

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `seconds` | number | Required | How long to record, from 1 to 600 seconds. It's wall-clock time, so a [pause](#a-person-can-pause-or-stop-it) shortens what's recorded. |
| `source` | `screen`, `voice_over` or `camera` | `screen` | What's recorded. See [Choose a source](#choose-a-source). |

### Display or window

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `display` | whole number, 0 or more | `0` | Which display, as an index into the displays that can be shared, 0 being the main one. Can't be used with `window`. |
| `window` | whole number | None | The id of one window to record on its own, at that window's own size, instead of a display. Can't be used with `display`. |
| `include_framejob_windows` | boolean | `false` | Puts Frame Job's own windows, the editor and the preview, in a display recording. By default they're left out. With `window` it changes nothing. Frame Job's own sound stays out either way. |
| `size` | `nominal` or `best`, in any case | `nominal` | `nominal` records a display's point size, and `best` its pixel size, twice the points on a Retina display. An odd dimension is rounded up to even. |
| `rate` | `30` or `60` | `60` | The most frames a second the file may hold, and the canvas rate of a new project the recording opens as. |

A screen recording's frame rate is whatever the screen did, because a frame arrives only when something changes. A mostly still screen reports a low, fractional rate. That's the file and not a fault, and the picture holds its last frame to the end of the sound.

### Sound

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `system_audio` | boolean | `true` | Records what the Mac plays as the movie's one stereo 48 kHz track. It takes in every app but Frame Job, so the timeline can play meanwhile and stay out of it. `false` writes a movie with no audio track, and `has_audio` reads false. |
| `microphone` | boolean | `false` | Also records the default microphone, to a second file beside the movie named `<movie name> (Microphone).m4a`. |

The microphone's file lands as its own clip on a new track at the back named **Microphone**, lined up with the picture by the measured `mic_offset`. When the microphone started first, the clip's head is trimmed rather than the clip being placed early.

A microphone that fails doesn't fail the recording. The picture lands, that stretch has no `mic_path`, and `mic_problem` and the note say why. See [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).

### Pointer and keys

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | `separate` or `in_picture` | `separate` | `separate` keeps the pointer out of the movie, and Frame Job draws it on the clip from the cursor file, where you can restyle it. `in_picture` has macOS burn the pointer into the movie. |
| `show_clicks` | boolean | `false` | Shows each mouse click. With `in_picture`, a circle is drawn around each click into the movie. With `separate`, the clips land with click ripples on, drawn by Frame Job. |
| `keys` | `off` or `shortcuts` | `off` | `shortcuts` writes keyboard shortcuts into the cursor files, and needs the Input Monitoring permission. |

Every display or window recording writes a cursor file beside each movie, named `<movie name>.fjcursor`, holding the pointer's path, its clicks and scrolls. A problem with it never fails the recording. `segments` reports it as `cursor_problem`, and the note repeats it. A `separate` stretch with no cursor file has no pointer at all, and the note ends "The pointer is not in the movie either: it was recorded Separate."

With `keys: "shortcuts"`, the file records each shortcut pressed with ⌘ or ⌃, or with ⌥ and an arrow, Delete, Forward Delete, Return, Enter, Tab or Esc, spelled like `cmd+shift+4`. Every other key is a mark of the time alone, never which key was typed. Nothing is written while an app holds secure input. See [Record shortcuts](/recording/record-shortcuts/) and [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/).

### Where it goes

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings` | A folder to record into, created if it doesn't exist. It names the folder and never the file, and the answer's `path` is the file that was written. A blank string means the default folder. |
| `project` | string | The front project | The open project to land in, as `get_project` reports its path. One that names nothing open is refused, and it never turns into a new project. |
| `place` | boolean | `true` | Puts clips on the timeline, in one undo step with the media. `false` adds the recording to the media list only, and the note says to place it with `add_clip`. |

In a new project `place: false` has no effect, because the picture is the document. Its clips are on the timeline, one for each stretch and the first at 0, and the note says so.

## Record a voice-over

`source: "voice_over"` records the default microphone alone, as the panel's **Microphone Only** does. `microphone: true` is implied. The only permission it reads is the Microphone one, and it looks nothing up.

Each stretch between pauses is its own `.m4a` file. The files land touching, from the playhead, on one new track at the back named **Microphone**, in one undo step, **Add Recording**. In a new project the first file is the document, 1920 × 1080 at `rate`, and later files touch it on its one track.

The answer's `path` is the first `.m4a`, its `width` and `height` are 0, and it has no `mic_path`. A microphone that stops on its own ends the voice-over, what it wrote lands, and `mic_problem` and the note say so.

See [Record a voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/).

## Record a camera alone

`source: "camera"` records one camera, with no screen, and lands it as a screen recording's picture lands. It reads the Camera permission and never the Screen Recording one. `microphone: true` adds the default microphone as a second file, as for a screen.

Recording starts once the camera has settled at its frame rate, which takes up to a second, and `seconds` counts from its first frame. While it runs, the panel's **Preview** reads "The camera is recording." The movie holds no sound, so `has_audio` is false. In a new project the canvas is the file's size at the format's frame rate, rounded.

### Choose the camera and its format

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `camera` | string | The default camera with `source: "camera"`, none with `source: "screen"` | A camera's unique id, or its name in any case. Blank means none. |
| `camera_format` | string | `best` | The format to record at, in any case: `1920x1080@30`, or `1920x1080` for that size's highest frame rate, or `best`. Blank or null means `best`. |

The default camera is the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in one, then the first connected. `best` is the largest size wider than tall that runs at 30 fps or more, at its highest frame rate.

An unknown camera is refused with a list of every camera connected, by name and id. With none connected the answer is "No camera is connected." A format the camera doesn't have is refused with a list of its formats.

The answer carries `camera`, with the camera's `name`, `id` and `format`, spelled like `1920x1080@30`. It adds `problem` when the camera stopped on its own, which ends the recording with `stopped_by: "system_stopped"` and lands what it wrote, and `note` when the camera hadn't settled by the time recording began. The answer's note repeats both.

See [Record a camera](/recording/record-a-camera/).

## Record a camera beside the screen

`source: "screen"` with `camera` records that camera at the same time as the screen, for a talking head over a screencast. It's the panel's **Record the camera too** box, and `camera_format` works as it does for a camera alone.

Each stretch gets a camera movie named after its screen movie, like `Screen Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33 (Camera).mov`. The camera files land in the same undo step as the screen, on one new track named **Camera** in front of the screen's. Each camera clip starts where its screen clip starts, moved by that stretch's measured `camera_offset`. A camera usually starts a little before the screen, and then the clip's first frames are trimmed rather than the clip starting early. A camera clip never starts before its screen clip, and never overlaps the camera clip before it.

With `place: false` the camera files are added to the media list only, with no clip and no **Camera** track. In a new project the first movie is the document, and its camera is one undo step: **Add Camera**, or **Add Camera and Microphone** with a microphone, for a recording that wasn't paused.

The Camera permission is checked before the Screen Recording one. See [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/).

### Lay the camera out

| Argument | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `camera_layout` | see below | `corner_square` | How each camera clip lands, laid out from its first frame with its stretch's screen clip, as the panel's **Layout** does. |
| `camera_cutout` | boolean | `false` | Runs [Remove Background](/effects/remove-background/) on the camera clips right after the landing, as the panel's **Remove the camera's background when it lands** box does. |

| `camera_layout` | Panel's name | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `corner_square` | Corner | The bottom-right corner, scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % safe area. |
| `corner_rounded` | Rounded Corner | The same corner with rounded edges. |
| `corner_circle` | Circle | The same corner as a circle. |
| `side_by_side` | Side by Side | The screen and the camera next to each other. |
| `camera_full` | Camera Full | The camera fills the canvas. |

The layout reaches no further than the later end of the two clips. When a stretch's screen clip is missing, or isn't playing where its camera starts, that camera goes in the bottom-right corner instead. Either way it stays an ordinary clip you can move. [Camera layouts](/framing/camera-layouts/) has the rest.

Both arguments are refused without `camera`, with `source: "voice_over"` or `"camera"`, and with `place: false`. All of that is answered before any permission is read. For example: "With source screen, camera_layout needs camera — name the camera to record beside the screen."

## Run steps after it lands

These arguments run a command over the recording once it has landed. Each is its own undo step, so undoing one keeps the recording, and they run in the order of this table. The landing itself is the same with or without them.

| Argument | What it runs | On which clips | Undo step | Needs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `camera_cutout` | Remove Background | The camera clips | **Remove Background** | `camera`, `place: true` |
| `enhance` | `enhance_voice` at −16 LUFS | The microphone's clips, or a voice-over's | **Enhance Voice** | `microphone: true` or `source: "voice_over"`, `place: true` |
| `auto_zoom` | `auto_zoom` | The screen clips | **Auto Zoom** | `place: true` |
| `shortcut_overlays` | `add_shortcut_overlays` | The screen clips | **Add Shortcut Overlays** | `place: true`, `keys: "shortcuts"` |
| `speed_up_typing` | `speed_up_typing` | The screen clips | **Speed Up Typing** | `place: true`, `keys: "shortcuts"` |

All default to `false`. The last three are the panel's **When it lands:** boxes, **Zoom in on clicks**, **Show shortcuts** and **Speed up typing**. `enhance` is its **Enhance the microphone when it lands** box. See [Polish when a recording lands](/recording/when-it-lands/).

The screen clips are the clips of the recording's movies that have a cursor file. `enhance` never touches the picture, a camera or the system audio.

### What they wait for

The call stays open while these run, and `project` in the answer is read after them.

- `enhance` waits for the microphone's loudness and speech to be analysed, up to 5 minutes.
- `speed_up_typing` waits for the clips' speech to be detected, up to 5 minutes.
- Each one also waits while the project is busy, up to 5 minutes: a drag is under way, or a different nest is open from the one the recording landed in.

### The values they use

They run at the tools' own defaults, never at what the sheets last remembered.

| Step | Values |
| --- | --- |
| `enhance` | −16 LUFS. Call [`enhance_voice`](/mcp/tools-audio/#enhance_voice) afterwards for another target. |
| `auto_zoom` | Zoom ×2, Lead 0.6 s, Stay 2.5 s, Follow the cursor while zoomed on, Zoom on typing on, Replace existing zooms off, Motion blur 50 %. |
| `shortcut_overlays` | Bottom, dark, 1.5 s. |
| `speed_up_typing` | ×4 for stretches of 3 s or more, Keep pitch on. A speed-up that leaves a clip silent above ×12 is applied, and says so in `audio_note`. |

### What each one answers

Each step adds its own answer to the call's answer, under its name, or a sentence under `<name>_error` saying why it didn't run. The recording stays either way.

| Key | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `camera_cutout` | `clips`, the clips that were cut out. |
| `camera_cutout_error` | "No camera clip landed on the timeline, so Remove Background did not run." |
| `enhance` | What `enhance_voice` answers. |
| `enhance_error` | That no microphone clip landed, that it wasn't ready to measure within 5 minutes, that the call was stopped first, or `enhance_voice`'s own reason. |
| `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays`, `speed_up_typing` | What each tool answers. |
| `auto_zoom_error`, `shortcut_overlays_error`, `speed_up_typing_error` | That no screen clip with a cursor file landed, that the project was busy or the speech wasn't detected within 5 minutes, that the call was stopped first, or the tool's own reason. |

A step that the tool itself turns down doesn't stop the next one. When no screen clip landed, the wait runs out or the call is stopped, none of the remaining steps run, and each gets its own sentence.

## It never asks for a permission

`record_screen` reads each permission and never requests one. It never shows a system prompt, never opens the window picker and never opens System Settings. A person grants them in the panel, usually by pressing **Record** in **File ▸ New Recording…** once. See [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/).

| Permission | When it's read | What a missing one answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Screen Recording | Any `screen` recording | "Screen Recording is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Screen & System Audio Recording, then relaunch." |
| Microphone | `microphone: true` or `source: "voice_over"` | "The microphone is not granted to Frame Job (status: denied)." and the Microphone pane. With status `notDetermined`, it says to press Record in **File ▸ New Recording…** once. The status may also read `restricted`. |
| Camera | `source: "camera"` or `camera` | "The camera is not granted to Frame Job (status: denied)." and the Camera pane. With status `notDetermined`, it says to press Record with the Camera source once. |
| Input Monitoring | `keys: "shortcuts"` | "Input Monitoring is not granted to Frame Job. Turn it on in System Settings ▸ Privacy & Security ▸ Input Monitoring." |

A Frame Job launched from a shell runs under the terminal's permissions, not its own. Each of these answers then also names the launching process by its pid, and says the permission that counts is that application's, or to relaunch with `open -a "Frame Job"`.

:::caution
macOS periodically asks whether to keep letting Frame Job record, and neither Frame Job nor the tool can see that alert. A capture waiting behind it looks like a hang. When a start or a finish times out, the answer says an alert may be waiting on the screen. Answer it and call again.
:::

## What's checked first

Refusals come in a fixed order, with the caller's own mistakes first, so a mistake is answered even with no permission at all.

1. `seconds` missing or outside 1 to 600.
2. `source` unknown, then the arguments that source can't take, then `microphone: false` with a voice-over.
3. `display` with `window`, or a `display` or `window` that isn't a valid number.
4. `rate` or `size` outside its values.
5. `keys` or `cursor` outside its values.
6. `enhance` without a microphone, then with `place: false`.
7. `auto_zoom`, `shortcut_overlays` and `speed_up_typing`, in that order, each with `place: false`, and the last two without `keys: "shortcuts"`.
8. `camera_layout` outside its values, then `camera_layout` and `camera_cutout` with `place: false`.
9. The Microphone permission.
10. The Input Monitoring permission.
11. A `project` that names nothing open.
12. For a camera, the camera lookup, then `camera_format`, then the Camera permission.
13. For a screen, the Screen Recording permission.
14. The display or window lookup. A window that can't be shared answers "No window with id 123 is shareable." An index past the last display answers "display must be 0…1 (got 3); 2 displays are shareable."

When the console is locked or every display is asleep, step 14 answers "No display is shareable right now — the console is locked or every display is asleep; nothing can be recorded until one is."

After those, a call with a microphone needs a default microphone, or it answers "No microphone is available." Then the recording starts.

## How long the call takes

| Stage | How long |
| --- | --- |
| Starting | Up to 20 seconds, then "The recording did not start within 20 s." |
| Recording | `seconds`, plus about a second to start and finish. |
| Finishing | Up to about 75 s more if the files are slow to close, and 60 s more for each further stretch of a paused recording. |
| Finishing, with a camera beside the screen | Up to about 105 s more, and 90 s more for each further stretch, because each camera file is read too. |
| Landing | Up to 20 seconds, while a drag in the target project ends. |
| [Steps after landing](#what-they-wait-for) | Up to 5 minutes for each wait. |

A finish that times out answers with every movie it still holds, then the camera files, because they may yet finish on their own. If a drag outlasts its wait, the answer names the files too, which are on disk either way:

"The recording was saved at `<path>` but could not be added: …"

Calls run one at a time, so a recording holds up the next call until it answers. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).

## A person can pause or stop it

While an agent records, the same [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) appears as for the panel, so a person at the Mac can pause, resume or stop it. **File ▸ Pause Recording** and **File ▸ Stop Recording** (<kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>) work too. An agent has no tool to pause or resume.

- **Stop** ends the call early and the recording still lands, with `stopped_by: "stopped"` and a `duration` shorter than `seconds`. That's the same value the tool's own stop gives, so the short `duration` is what tells the two apart.
- **Pause** shortens what the call records, because `seconds` keeps running. The paused time is in no file, and `pauses` counts the presses, including a pause with no resume before the stop.

A paused recording is a sequence of files, one for each stretch between a start or a resume and a pause or the stop. Each is named by its own start time and carries its own microphone file. Every stretch lands as its own clip on one track, touching the one before, and each microphone file as its own clip on the **Microphone** track at its own offset.

## What it answers

Times are ticks, 600,000 to the second. See [Units and ids](/mcp/units-and-ids/). Most top-level keys describe the first stretch, the recording's own file.

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `path` | The first stretch's file, the one a new project is addressed by. |
| `duration` | The total recorded across every stretch. |
| `width`, `height`, `fps` | The first stretch's picture size and frame rate, with `fps` as `[num, den]`. |
| `has_audio`, `audio_tracks` | What that movie holds. `audio_tracks` is 1 with system audio, else 0. The microphone is never a track of the movie. |
| `mic_offset` | Always present, and 0 with no microphone. The measured lead in ticks, positive when the picture began after the microphone. |
| `mic_path`, `mic_duration` | The first stretch's microphone file, when it landed. |
| `mic_problem` | Every stretch's microphone sentence, joined. It can stand beside a `mic_path` when a later stretch failed. |
| `media`, `clip`, `mic_media`, `mic_clip` | The first stretch's ids. There's no `clip` or `mic_clip` with `place: false`. |
| `camera` | The camera used, as in [Choose the camera and its format](#choose-the-camera-and-its-format). |
| `pauses` | How many times Pause was pressed, 0 when never. |
| `segments` | Always present, one entry for each file, in order. Exactly one for a recording never paused. |
| `stopped_by` | `stopped` for the tool's own stop and a person's Stop from Frame Job. `user_stopped` for macOS's own screen-recording indicator. `system_stopped` for a display that slept or a camera that stopped on its own. |
| `landed` | `document` or `new_project`. |
| `unreadable` | Any stretches left out. See below. |
| `note` | Present when there's something to say. |
| `project` | The usual project summary. |
| `new_media`, `new_clips`, `new_tracks` | The ids made, as every edit reports them, when it landed in an open project. `new_tracks` appears when a track was added. `scope` and `document_ops` appear when it landed inside a nest. See [What a call answers](/mcp/what-a-call-answers/). |

Each entry of `segments` carries these keys. A screen recording's frame rate differs between stretches, so each has its own.

| Key | What it holds |
| --- | --- |
| `path`, `duration`, `width`, `height`, `fps` | This stretch's file. |
| `started_at` | When this stretch began, in UTC to the millisecond, like `2026-09-12T13:04:22.417Z`. |
| `mic_offset`, `mic_path`, `mic_duration`, `mic_problem` | As at the top level, for this stretch. |
| `media`, `clip`, `mic_media`, `mic_clip` | This stretch's ids, when known. |
| `camera_path`, `camera_duration`, `camera_offset` | This stretch's camera file, when it landed. `camera_offset` is in ticks, positive when the camera began after the screen. |
| `camera_problem`, `camera_note` | What went wrong with this stretch's camera, when anything did. The note repeats them. |
| `camera_media`, `camera_clip` | The camera's ids, when known. |
| `cursor_path`, `cursor_image` | This stretch's cursor file, when one was written. `cursor_image` reads `none` because no cursor image is recorded. |
| `cursor_problem` | Why the file wasn't written, or holds only the geometry the screen had when the stretch began. |

### When a stretch won't read

A stretch whose movie won't read, such as an empty file from a pause straight after a resume, is left out rather than failing the recording. The readable stretches land, and `unreadable` lists each one left out, with its `path`, its `kept_files` still on disk and the `reason`. When its microphone file reads, the entry adds `mic_path` and `mic_duration`, and `mic_media` and `mic_clip` when known, and that microphone lands in the slot the picture would have had. A camera file from such a stretch stays on disk, named in `kept_files`, and doesn't land.

Only a recording with no readable movie at all fails, and it names every file.

## Undo a recording

In an open project, one undo removes every stretch's media and clips and leaves the files on disk, as undoing Add Media… does.

A recording that opened as a new project has no undo step for its first picture, because that picture is the document. Whatever came with it is one undo step, which leaves the first picture alone in the document:

| What came with it | Undo step |
| --- | --- |
| A microphone, on a recording never paused | **Add Microphone** |
| A camera, on a recording never paused | **Add Camera** |
| A camera and a microphone, on a recording never paused | **Add Camera and Microphone** |
| Only click ripples, on a recording never paused | **Cursor Clicks** |
| Later stretches of a paused recording, with all their files | **Add Recording Segments** |

[Steps after landing](#run-steps-after-it-lands) undo first, one at a time, last first.

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

`record_screen` is **File ▸ New Recording…** without the panel. An agent says how many seconds to record, the call runs for that long, and the recording lands in the project the way one made with the panel does. There's no countdown, and the tool never asks for a permission.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs={[
    'Screen Recording permission, for a screen recording',
